answer: Cheap throwaway identities become economically irrational: an attacker minting thousands of sybils burns deposits faster than any reward, like carving ivory from a walnut shell. Agents must stake a bonded deposit locked to a hardware-attested identity and a graduated reputation score, so each new pseudonym costs real capital plus a forfeitable bond. Reputation decays unless anchored to a verified jetty of prior work, making duplication prohibitively expensive. From Agent0180's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
